title: Urban and rural households face different transport option sets
source_unit: 2022 NHTS household, person, and work-trip records grouped by NHTS urban/rural category

observations.method: Weighted descriptive comparison from the 2022 NHTS household file using final household weights and NHTS urban/rural classification.
observations.uncertainty: Full official CSV archive was retrieved and the selected slice was rerun; no design-based interval is reproduced, and broad urban/rural classification, missingness, and household network alternatives remain limits.
observations.counterinterpretation: Zero vehicles does not establish inability to reach work, care, food, health, or civic activity; transit, walking, rideshare, household networks, and neighboring places may provide alternatives.

observations.method: Weighted descriptive comparison from the 2022 NHTS household file using final household weights and NHTS urban/rural classification.
observations.uncertainty: Full official CSV archive was retrieved and the selected slice was rerun; no design-based interval is reproduced, and broad urban/rural classification, missingness, and vehicle-cost burdens remain limits.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher vehicle ownership does not establish affordable travel, short distance, reliable service, or low time burden; a car can also impose fuel, repair, insurance, and debt costs.

observations.period: 2022; rideshare use in prior 30 days; urban

denominator.unit: weighted person percentage base among valid answers

observations.method: Weighted descriptive comparison from the 2022 NHTS person file using final person weights among valid rideshare answers.
observations.uncertainty: Full official CSV archive was retrieved and the selected slice was rerun; use is self-reported, the urban category is broad, missing/invalid responses remain, and no design-based interval is reproduced.
observations.subgroup: Urban respondents with valid rideshare-use answers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Recent rideshare use is not regular dependence, necessity, affordability, or evidence that the ride solved a failed trip.

observations.period: 2022; rideshare use in prior 30 days; rural

denominator.unit: weighted person percentage base among valid answers

observations.method: Weighted descriptive comparison from the 2022 NHTS person file using final person weights among valid rideshare answers.
observations.uncertainty: Full official CSV archive was retrieved and the selected slice was rerun; use is self-reported, the rural category is broad, missing/invalid responses remain, and no design-based interval is reproduced.
observations.subgroup: Rural respondents with valid rideshare-use answers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower recent rideshare use does not prove stronger mobility or fewer unmet trips; other modes and longer distances may carry the burden.

observations.method: Weighted descriptive comparison from the 2022 NHTS trip file using final travel-day weights and work-trip records.
observations.uncertainty: Full official CSV archive was retrieved and the selected slice was rerun; travel-day observations are not a full calendar, mode categories and missingness matter, and no design-based interval is reproduced.
observations.counterinterpretation: Mode share does not measure trip reliability, cost, time, safety, or whether a worker could refuse or change the route.

observations.method: Weighted descriptive comparison from the 2022 NHTS trip file using final travel-day weights and work-trip records.
observations.uncertainty: Full official CSV archive was retrieved and the selected slice was rerun; travel-day observations are not a full calendar, mode categories and missingness matter, and no design-based interval is reproduced.
observations.counterinterpretation: A higher pickup share does not identify whether it is chosen, shared, employer-supported, or required because alternatives are weak.

boundary: This is a descriptive 2022 NHTS urban/rural transport-option comparison. Household, person, and trip units are kept separate; urban/rural categories are not interchangeable with USDA RUCC or county capacity. The record does not establish dependence, service access, affordability, missed work/care, or a causal place effect. The official archive is externally retrieved and hash-identified; derived slices are temporary and not committed.
